questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You log on using personal Unito username and password. Then you fill in your Career plan by adding the courses you plan to follow. The Career plan must be identical to the approved learning agreement (approved by UCPH). You can easily modify the plan during your stay. You register each course at the individual site

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Good guidance douments available on-line.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No problem, simply follow the guidance.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use time to read the gudiances available, and just follow them. Do not be afraid of changing courses during your stay, just remember to update Career plan

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fairly satisfied. Each professor has his/her way of teaching. Some ways are better than others. But I learned a lot, no mater the different styles, that in some cases were less inspiring.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High level. Content and language.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. At Unito you follow lectures, each course 6 hours a week, in blocks a 2 hours or 3 hours. Mostly without breaks, although I did experience a 5 min coffe breake in a 3-hour course. You hang in, listen and try to understand. No debate during lectures, no reading before, and sometimes no slides available after. In comparison to UCPH you are supposed to remember and learn all, and at the exam discuss the theme with the proffessors without notes available.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Letteratura italiana (12 cfu). Grammatica italiana (6 cfu), Storia del cinema (6 cfu), Dialettologia (6 cfu) and Stilistica e metrica (6 cfu). I changed the last course to grammatica, as it was too difficult.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choose after interest and be curious. If interesting it is easier to follow. Take time to read the course descriptions.

questions.answer: Rowing

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the museums, walk in the nature, drink coffee. Take the train to Milano, to Genova. Se the castles around Torino. See San Sacre Michele. Talk to the people you meet on your way.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them during class. Ask for advice and help.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, but the language at some of the lectures.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: No parts specificly. I loved it all.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take time to do the paper work; Follow lectures even if you do not understand all; have an open mind when it comes to the exam process.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even when it is hard it is a valuable experince.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The possibility to follow specific courses, and get a profound knowledge on a subject.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had too many hours per week the first half of the semester. I managed my many hours/week, but I was extremly challenged. I should have cancelled/canged one course from the begining.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do not fear the exams. The process is extremely different from the one at UCPH, but ask your fellow studens for advice and experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
